messages.subject: Rendering MathML
parts: I'm having a problem with MathJax/HTML/MathML output not rendering correctly. I've put an MWE up at http://pastebin.com/rKY0uPv5. When I run that app, I get the raw HTML/MML displayed instead of rendered output. However, if I copy that raw output to https://www.mathjax.org/ (Modular Input & Output > Try a live demo), it renders exactly as I want. This behavior exists for me in both Chrome and Firefox. If it matters, I'm running R 3.2.2 and shiny 0.12.2. I've also made sure to follow the example at http://shiny.rstudio.com/gallery/mathjax.html (specifically, uiOutput in ui, renderUI in server, and withMathJax wrapped around the output in server). Would anyone happen to know why raw HTML/MML code is being displayed instead of rendered output?

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Rendering MathML
parts:
This line:

return(withMathJax(output))

should be this instead:

return(withMathJax(HTML(output)))

The HTML() tells us that `output` is intended to be interpreted as raw markup, instead of text. We always have to assume text unless told otherwise, because while interpreting markup as text is broken and ugly, interpreting text as markup is often a difficult-to-detect security issue which is much worse.

Even with HTML() in place, the output doesn't look right, but I'm afraid I'm not conversant enough in MathML to help.

It might be easier to debug if you compose your mathjax using functions instead of pasting strings together. This video will give you the background:

However, the MathML elements are not part of the Shiny tag vocabulary, so you'll have to create your own MathML functions:

math <- function(...) tag("math", list(...))
mtable <- function(...) tag("mtable", list(...))
mtr <- function(...) tag("mtr", list(...))

etc.

Then you can do things like:

math(
  mtable(
    lapply(data, function(x) {
      mtr(...)
    })
  )
)

You can call print() on such objects to see the generated markup at the R console.

messages.subject: Re: Rendering MathML
parts:
Changing the return statement to return(withMathJax(HTML(output))) did help but, as you noted, still left the rendered output looking strange.

After looking into the raw code a little more, I made a discovery that actually fixed everything (as far as I can tell). Within the raw code that I was pasting together, there were instances of something like this: <mtext><mrow><mtext>cbGroup1:cb3; cb4:</mtext></mrow></mtext>; in particular, <mrow><mtext> tags inside <mtext> tags. Once I removed the inner <mrow><mtext> tags (i.e., changed that example bit of code to <mtext>cbGroup1:cb3; cb4:</mtext>), Shiny rendered the output correctly.

It seems, then, the live demo on MathJax.org may be a little more tolerant/understanding of MathML than Shiny. All in all, however, my Shiny app is working well now and I'm quite happy it only took a relatively minor tweak of my code to get it to that point.
